models.name: Random targeting
models.description: Treat a uniformly random fraction of users. Its expected gain is the population-average effect times the fraction treated.

models.name: Response propensity
models.description: Targets the users most likely to produce the outcome when treated. It ignores what they would have done anyway, which is exactly the gap uplift models aim to close.

models.name: Two-model (logistic)
models.description: Two independent logistic regressions on standardised features, one per arm; uplift is the difference of predicted probabilities. A linear, transparent baseline.

models.name: T-learner (gradient boosting)
models.description: Same two-model construction with gradient-boosted trees as the base learner, so non-linearities and interactions are captured within each arm.

models.name: S-learner (gradient boosting)
models.description: One gradient-boosted model on features plus the treatment indicator; uplift is the prediction with treatment=1 minus the prediction with treatment=0.

selection.rule: Highest validation gain over random on the covariate-adjusted basis, among models that estimate uplift.

leakage_controls: Splits are a salted hash of row_id: every row is in exactly one of train / valid / test.
Models are fitted on train rows only; validation selects the champion; test is used once for reporting.
Doubly-robust evaluation scores are cross-fitted: no row is scored by a nuisance model that saw it.
Gradient-boosting early stopping uses an internal 10% hold-out of the training rows, not valid/test.

evaluation_bases.unadjusted: Treated minus control outcome rate within the targeted group.
evaluation_bases.adjusted: Mean cross-fitted doubly-robust (AIPW) score within the targeted group.
